title: God uses broken people.
paragraphs: God uses broken people.
That is the scandal of grace.

He used Moses with his fear.
David with his failure.
Peter with his denial.
Paul with his past.
God has never been limited by human weakness.
But He does resist something.
Pride.
James 4:6 says, “God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.”
That means brokenness is not the barrier.
Pride is.

You can be wounded and still be chosen.
You can be flawed and still be called.
You can be weak and still be useful in the hands of God.
But if your heart refuses correction, refuses repentance, refuses surrender, you are fighting the very grace you claim to need.

God is near to the contrite.
He revives the crushed in spirit.
He heals the one who stops pretending.

But the proud person wants mercy without repentance.
Blessing without bowing.
Power without holiness.
A platform without a cross.
And God will not endorse that.

This is the dividing line:
Brokenness says, “Lord, I need You.”
Pride says, “Lord, I can manage without You.”

One posture gets grace.
The other gets resistance.
So no, your scars do not disqualify you.

Your sin can be forgiven.
Your past can be redeemed.
Your shame can be washed clean.
But only when you come low before Jesus Christ.
The gospel is not that good people earn God’s favor.
The gospel is that sinners, humbled by the truth, repent and run to Christ.

We are all broken by sin.
We all stand guilty before a holy God.
We cannot save ourselves by effort, image, religion, or pride.

But Jesus came.
He lived the righteous life we could not live.
He died the death our sins deserved.
He rose again in victory.
And now grace is offered to every person who will repent and believe.

Not to the self-exalting.
Not to the self-justifying.
But to the humble.
So bring God your broken heart.
Just do not bring Him your pride.
Because the same God who resists the proud will pour mercy on the one who falls at His feet.

Reflection:
Have I been offering God my pain while still protecting my pride?
Save this as a reminder: God can heal what is broken, but He will first humble what is proud.
Advanced teachings. Growing daily.

Shame doesn’t get the final word.
We Write Stories that Shame Tried to Erase.
